451	        elif before["nullable"] and not after["nullable"]:
452	            kind = "nullable_tightened"
453	        else:
454	            continue
455	
456	        # The base version always has the broken field; the target version's
457	        # same-named field joins the traversal only when it still exists.
458	        start_ids = [_field_id_by_name(conn, base_row["id"], name)]
459	        if after is not None:

463	        )
464	
465	        breaking_changes.append(
466	            {
467	                "field": name,
468	                "kind": kind,
469	                "before": before,
470	                "after": after,
471	                "impacted": impacted,
472	            }
473	        )
474	    return breaking_changes

548	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
549	) -> dict:
550	    """Read-only summary of adjacent-version breaking changes and impact.
551	
552	    One entry per adjacent version pair of the dataset, ordered by base
553	    version number ascending; a pair with no breaking change is listed with
554	    zero counts. The breaking entries of a pair are exactly those of
555	    :func:`check_schema_version_compatibility_impact` (``removed``,
556	    ``type_changed`` or ``nullable_tightened``, several changes of one field
557	    collapsing into a single entry) and ``breaking_count`` is their number.
558	    The pair's impacted set is the union of every entry's downstream fields —
559	    same start-field rule as the pairwise impact response, merged and
560	    deduplicated, never containing a start field itself (cycles terminate) —
561	    and ``impacted_count`` is its size; ``impacted_datasets`` lists the
562	    distinct dataset names appearing in it, sorted ascending. ``totals``
563	    counts the pairs and sums the per-pair breaking and deduplicated impacted
564	    counts over the whole dataset. A dataset with fewer than two versions
565	    yields an empty pair list and all-zero totals, never an error.
566	
567	    The summary is recomputed from the persisted definitions and lineage
568	    mappings on every read: it caches nothing and never writes, so version
569	    definitions, lineage mappings and the impact cache are all left
570	    untouched, and quality or privacy state plays no role. The dataset
571	    resolves first (404); any request body bytes (including whitespace-only
572	    bytes) or any query parameter is a 422 checked afterwards, and every
573	    ordering is computed explicitly rather than read from database order.
574	    """
575	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
576	
577	    if body:
578	        raise RequestInvalidError(
579	            "The schema evolution summary endpoint does not accept a "
580	            "request body"
581	        )
582	    if query_keys:
583	        raise RequestInvalidError(
584	            "The schema evolution summary endpoint does not accept query "
585	            "parameters"
586	        )
587	
588	    version_rows = conn.execute(
589	        "SELECT id, version FROM schema_versions WHERE dataset_id = ?",
590	        (dataset["id"],),
591	    ).fetchall()
592	    ordered = sorted(version_rows, key=lambda row: row["version"])
593	
594	    pairs: list[dict] = []
595	    for base_row, target_row in zip(ordered, ordered[1:]):
596	        breaking_changes = _breaking_changes_with_impact(conn, base_row, target_row)
597	        impacted_refs = {
598	            (item["dataset"], item["version"], item["field"])
599	            for change in breaking_changes
600	            for item in change["impacted"]
601	        }
602	        pairs.append(
603	            {
604	                "base_version": base_row["version"],
605	                "target_version": target_row["version"],
606	                "breaking_count": len(breaking_changes),
607	                "impacted_count": len(impacted_refs),
608	                "impacted_datasets": sorted({ref[0] for ref in impacted_refs}),
609	            }
610	        )
611	
612	    totals = {
613	        "pair_count": len(pairs),
614	        "breaking_count": sum(pair["breaking_count"] for pair in pairs),
615	        "impacted_count": sum(pair["impacted_count"] for pair in pairs),
616	    }
617	    return {"dataset": dataset["name"], "pairs": pairs, "totals": totals}

625	def _field_status_change(before: dict | None, after: dict | None) -> str:
626	    """Status literal of one field between two adjacent versions.
627	
628	    The literals reuse the breaking-entry vocabulary of the compatibility
629	    check (``removed``, ``type_changed``, ``nullable_tightened``) extended
630	    with the non-breaking outcomes: ``added`` when the field appears on the
631	    target side, ``nullable_loosened`` when only the nullability relaxes and
632	    ``unchanged`` when both definitions agree (including both absent).
633	    Several changes of one field collapse into a single status, a type
634	    change winning over a nullable tightening (mirrors the breaking-entry
635	    rule of the compatibility check).
636	    """
637	    if before is None:
638	        return "added" if after is not None else "unchanged"
639	    if after is None:
640	        return "removed"
641	    if before == after:
642	        return "unchanged"
643	    if before["type"] != after["type"]:
644	        return "type_changed"
645	    if before["nullable"] and not after["nullable"]:
646	        return "nullable_tightened"
647	    return "nullable_loosened"

650	def get_field_trajectory(
651	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
652	    dataset_name: str,
653	    field_name: str,
654	    *,
655	    body: bytes = b"",
656	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
657	) -> dict:
658	    """Read-only cross-version trajectory of one field of a dataset.
659	
660	    ``entries`` lists every schema version of the dataset ordered by version
661	    number ascending, each carrying the field's persisted definition in that
662	    version (only ``type`` and ``nullable``) or ``None`` — key retained —
663	    when the field does not exist there. ``changes`` lists one entry per
664	    adjacent version pair, ordered by base version ascending; each entry
665	    carries the pair's ``status`` (see :func:`_field_status_change`) and the
666	    field's downstream impact for that pair, computed with the same
667	    start-field rule as the compatibility impact response: the traversal
668	    starts from the base version's same-named field and, when the field
669	    exists in the target version, also from the target version's field. The
670	    impacted set is deduplicated, never contains a start field itself
671	    (cycles terminate), is sorted by dataset, version and field ascending
672	    and is empty when the field has no downstream; ``impacted_datasets``
673	    lists the distinct dataset names appearing in it, sorted ascending. A
674	    dataset with fewer than two versions yields an empty change list, never
675	    an error.
676	
677	    Only the persisted version field definitions and lineage mappings are
678	    read; quality, privacy, snapshot and processing-task state play no
679	    role. The trajectory is recomputed on every read: it caches nothing and
680	    never writes, so version definitions, lineage mappings and the impact
681	    cache are all left untouched, and every ordering is computed explicitly
682	    rather than read from database order.
683	
684	    The dataset resolves first (404), then the field must appear in at
685	    least one of the dataset's versions (404); any request body bytes
686	    (including whitespace-only bytes) or any query parameter is a 422
687	    checked afterwards, so both 404 cases keep precedence over the request
688	    shape checks (mirroring the evolution summary endpoint).
689	    """
690	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
691	
692	    version_rows = conn.execute(
693	        "SELECT id, version FROM schema_versions WHERE dataset_id = ?",
694	        (dataset["id"],),
695	    ).fetchall()
696	    ordered = sorted(version_rows, key=lambda row: row["version"])
697	    definitions = [
698	        _version_field_definitions(conn, row["id"]) for row in ordered
699	    ]
700	    if not any(field_name in fields for fields in definitions):
701	        raise NotFoundError(
702	            f"Field '{field_name}' does not exist in any schema version of "
703	            f"dataset '{dataset_name}'"
704	        )
705	
706	    if body:
707	        raise RequestInvalidError(
708	            "The field trajectory endpoint does not accept a request body"
709	        )
710	    if query_keys:
711	        raise RequestInvalidError(
712	            "The field trajectory endpoint does not accept query parameters"
713	        )
714	
715	    entries = [
716	        {"version": row["version"], "definition": fields.get(field_name)}
717	        for row, fields in zip(ordered, definitions)
718	    ]
719	
720	    changes: list[dict] = []
721	    for index, (base_row, target_row) in enumerate(zip(ordered, ordered[1:])):
722	        before = definitions[index].get(field_name)
723	        after = definitions[index + 1].get(field_name)
724	        # The base version's same-named field starts the traversal when it
725	        # exists; the target version's joins when it exists (the same
726	        # start-field rule as the compatibility impact response).
727	        start_ids = []
728	        if before is not None:
729	            start_ids.append(_field_id_by_name(conn, base_row["id"], field_name))
730	        if after is not None:
731	            start_ids.append(
732	                _field_id_by_name(conn, target_row["id"], field_name)
733	            )
734	        impacted = _compute_impacted_multi(
735	            conn, [field_id for field_id in start_ids if field_id is not None]
736	        )
737	        changes.append(
738	            {
739	                "base_version": base_row["version"],
740	                "target_version": target_row["version"],
741	                "status": _field_status_change(before, after),
742	                "impacted": impacted,
743	                "impacted_datasets": sorted(
744	                    {item["dataset"] for item in impacted}
745	                ),
746	            }
747	        )
748	
749	    return {
750	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
751	        "field": field_name,
752	        "entries": entries,
753	        "changes": changes,
754	    }

792	def create_lineage_link(
793	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
794	    *,
795	    target_dataset: str,
796	    target_version: int,
797	    target_field: str,
798	    source_dataset: str,
799	    source_version: int,
800	    source_field: str,
801	) -> dict:
802	    target = require_dataset(conn, target_dataset, role="Target dataset")
803	    source = require_dataset(conn, source_dataset, role="Source dataset")
804	
805	    if source["id"] == target["id"]:
806	        raise RequestInvalidError("Source and target datasets must be different")
807	
808	    target_version_id, target_field_id = _require_field(
809	        conn, target, target_version, target_field, role="Target"
810	    )
811	    source_version_id, source_field_id = _require_field(
812	        conn, source, source_version, source_field, role="Source"
813	    )
814	
815	    existing = conn.execute(
816	        "SELECT id FROM lineage_links WHERE target_field_id = ? AND source_field_id = ?",
817	        (target_field_id, source_field_id),
818	    ).fetchone()
819	    if existing is not None:
820	        raise ConflictError(
821	            "This field mapping has already been registered: "
822	            f"'{source_dataset}' v{source_version}.{source_field} -> "
823	            f"'{target_dataset}' v{target_version}.{target_field}"
824	        )
825	
826	    try:
827	        conn.execute(
828	            "INSERT INTO lineage_links ("
829	            "target_dataset_id, target_version_id, target_field_id, "
830	            "source_dataset_id, source_version_id, source_field_id, created_at"
831	            ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
832	            (
833	                target["id"],
834	                target_version_id,
835	                target_field_id,
836	                source["id"],
837	                source_version_id,
838	                source_field_id,
839	                utc_now_iso(),
840	            ),
841	        )
842	    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
843	        raise ConflictError("This field mapping has already been registered") from exc
844	
845	    # The new edge can only extend the impact of fields that reach its source.
846	    _invalidate_impact_cache_for_upstream(
847	        conn, source["name"], source_version, source_field, source_field_id
848	    )
849	
850	    return {
851	        "target_dataset": target["name"],
852	        "target_version": target_version,
853	        "target_field": target_field,
854	        "source": {
855	            "dataset": source["name"],
856	            "version": source_version,
857	            "field": source_field,
858	        },
859	    }

922	def _lineage_forward_edges(
923	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
924	) -> dict[int, list[tuple[int, dict]]]:
925	    """Adjacency of the lineage graph: source field id -> target field refs."""
926	    rows = conn.execute(
927	        """
928	        SELECT  ll.source_field_id AS source_field_id,
929	                ll.target_field_id AS target_field_id,
930	                td.name            AS target_dataset,
931	                tv.version         AS target_version,
932	                tf.name            AS target_field
933	        FROM    lineage_links ll
934	        JOIN    datasets td ON td.id = ll.target_dataset_id
935	        JOIN    schema_versions tv ON tv.id = ll.target_version_id
936	        JOIN    schema_fields tf ON tf.id = ll.target_field_id
937	        """
938	    ).fetchall()
939	    edges: dict[int, list[tuple[int, dict]]] = {}
940	    for row in rows:
941	        ref = {
942	            "dataset": row["target_dataset"],
943	            "version": row["target_version"],
944	            "field": row["target_field"],
945	        }
946	        edges.setdefault(row["source_field_id"], []).append(
947	            (row["target_field_id"], ref)
948	        )
949	    return edges
950	
951	
952	def _compute_impacted(conn: sqlite3.Connection, source_field_id: int) -> list[dict]:
953	    """All fields reachable downstream of the source, deduplicated and sorted.
954	
955	    The source field id is seeded into the visited set, so cycles terminate
956	    and the source itself never appears in the result.
957	    """
958	    edges = _lineage_forward_edges(conn)
959	    visited = {source_field_id}
960	    impacted: dict[tuple[str, int, str], dict] = {}
961	    queue = [source_field_id]
962	    while queue:
963	        current = queue.pop()
964	        for target_field_id, ref in edges.get(current, ()):
965	            if target_field_id in visited:
966	                continue
967	            visited.add(target_field_id)
968	            impacted[(ref["dataset"], ref["version"], ref["field"])] = ref
969	            queue.append(target_field_id)
970	    return [impacted[key] for key in sorted(impacted)]

973	def _impact_cache_lookup(
974	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, dataset: str, version: int, field: str
975	) -> list[dict] | None:
976	    row = conn.execute(
977	        "SELECT impacted FROM lineage_impact_cache "
978	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ? AND source_field = ?",
979	        (dataset, version, field),
980	    ).fetchone()
981	    return None if row is None else json.loads(row["impacted"])

984	def _impact_cache_store(
985	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
986	    dataset: str,
987	    version: int,
988	    field: str,
989	    impacted: list[dict],
990	) -> None:
991	    conn.execute(
992	        "DELETE FROM lineage_impact_cache "
993	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ? AND source_field = ?",
994	        (dataset, version, field),
995	    )

997	        "INSERT INTO lineage_impact_cache ("
998	        "source_dataset, source_version, source_field, impacted, created_at"
999	        ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
1000	        (dataset, version, field, json.dumps(impacted), utc_now_iso()),
1001	    )
1002	    cache_id = cursor.lastrowid
1003	    mentioned = {dataset} | {item["dataset"] for item in impacted}
1004	    conn.executemany(
1005	        "INSERT INTO lineage_impact_cache_datasets (cache_id, dataset) "
1006	        "VALUES (?, ?)",

1023	def _invalidate_impact_cache_for_upstream(
1024	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1025	    source_dataset: str,
1026	    source_version: int,
1027	    source_field: str,
1028	    source_field_id: int,
1029	) -> None:
1030	    """Invalidate cached impacts of the new link's source and its upstream.
1031	
1032	    A new mapping ``source -> target`` only changes the impact result of
1033	    fields that can reach ``source`` (``source`` itself included), so exactly
1034	    those cached entries are dropped; unrelated entries are kept. The reverse
1035	    walk runs after the link was inserted so cycles are covered too.
1036	    """
1037	    rows = conn.execute(
1038	        """
1039	        SELECT  ll.target_field_id AS target_field_id,
1040	                ll.source_field_id AS source_field_id,
1041	                sd.name            AS source_dataset,
1042	                sv.version         AS source_version,
1043	                sf.name            AS source_field
1044	        FROM    lineage_links ll
1045	        JOIN    datasets sd ON sd.id = ll.source_dataset_id
1046	        JOIN    schema_versions sv ON sv.id = ll.source_version_id
1047	        JOIN    schema_fields sf ON sf.id = ll.source_field_id
1048	        """
1049	    ).fetchall()
1050	    reverse: dict[int, list[sqlite3.Row]] = {}
1051	    for row in rows:
1052	        reverse.setdefault(row["target_field_id"], []).append(row)
1053	
1054	    visited = {source_field_id}
1055	    upstream = {(source_dataset, source_version, source_field)}
1056	    queue = [source_field_id]
1057	    while queue:
1058	        current = queue.pop()
1059	        for row in reverse.get(current, ()):
1060	            if row["source_field_id"] in visited:
1061	                continue
1062	            visited.add(row["source_field_id"])
1063	            upstream.add(
1064	                (row["source_dataset"], row["source_version"], row["source_field"])
1065	            )
1066	            queue.append(row["source_field_id"])
1067	
1068	    conn.executemany(
1069	        "DELETE FROM lineage_impact_cache "
1070	        "WHERE source_dataset = ? AND source_version = ? AND source_field = ?",
1071	        sorted(upstream),
1072	    )
1073	
1074	
1075	def get_lineage_impact(
1076	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, dataset_name: str, version: int, field: str
1077	) -> dict:
1078	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
1079	    _, field_id = _require_field(conn, dataset, version, field, role="Source")
1080	
1081	    impacted = _impact_cache_lookup(conn, dataset["name"], version, field)
1082	    if impacted is None:
1083	        impacted = _compute_impacted(conn, field_id)
1084	        _impact_cache_store(conn, dataset["name"], version, field, impacted)
1085	
1086	    return {
1087	        "source": {"dataset": dataset["name"], "version": version, "field": field},
1088	        "impacted": impacted,
1089	    }

1129	def _validate_rule_params(
1130	    kind: str, params: dict[str, Any], field_names: set[str]
1131	) -> None:
1132	    """Validate rule parameters structurally (422) and against the schema (404)."""
1133	
1134	    def require_existing_field(field_name: Any) -> str:
1135	        if not isinstance(field_name, str) or not field_name:
1136	            raise RequestInvalidError(
1137	                f"Rule kind '{kind}' requires a non-empty 'field' parameter"
1138	            )
1139	        if field_name not in field_names:
1140	            raise NotFoundError(f"Field '{field_name}' does not exist in this version")
1141	        return field_name
1142	
1143	    if kind == "not_null":
1144	        require_existing_field(params.get("field"))
1145	        return
1146

1308	def evaluate_quality_rules(
1309	    conn: sqlite3.Connection, dataset_name: str, version_number: int, rows: list[dict]
1310	) -> dict:
1311	    dataset = require_dataset(conn, dataset_name)
1312	    version_row = _require_schema_version(conn, dataset, version_number)
1313	
1314	    rule_rows = conn.execute(
1315	        "SELECT id, name, kind, params, enabled "
1316	        "FROM quality_rules WHERE version_id = ? AND enabled = 1 ORDER BY id",
1317	        (version_row["id"],),
1318	    ).fetchall()
1319	
1320	    results: list[dict] = []
1321	    for rule_row in rule_rows:
1322	        params = json.loads(rule_row["params"])
1323	        kind = rule_row["kind"]
1324	        violations: list[int] = []
1325	
1326	        if kind == "not_null":
1327	            field = params["field"]
1328	            violations = [
1329	                index
1330	                for index, row in enumerate(rows)
1331	                if _row_violates_not_null(row, field)
1332	            ]
1333	        elif kind == "numeric_range":
1334	            field = params["field"]
1335	            violations = [
1336	                index
1337	                for index, row in enumerate(rows)
1338	                if _row_violates_numeric_range(
1339	                    row, field, params["min"], params["max"]
1340	                )
1341	            ]
1342	        elif kind == "unique":
1343	            fields = params["fields"]
1344	            seen: dict[str, int] = {}
1345	            duplicated: set[int] = set()
1346	            for index, row in enumerate(rows):
1347	                combo = _row_violates_unique(row, fields)
1348	                key = _json_combo_key(combo)
1349	                if key in seen:
1350	                    duplicated.add(seen[key])
1351	                    duplicated.add(index)
1352	                else:
1353	                    seen[key] = index
1354	            violations = sorted(duplicated)
1355	
1356	        results.append(
1357	            {
1358	                "rule_id": rule_row["id"],
1359	                "name": rule_row["name"],
1360	                "passed": not violations,
1361	                "violations": violations,
1362	            }
1363	        )
1364	
1365	    # Every successful evaluation appends an immutable summary to the history
1366	    # (an empty submission is recorded too, with zero violations). A rejected
1367	    # or failed evaluation raises above and leaves no record.
1368	    _record_quality_rule_evaluation(
1369	        conn,
1370	        version_row["id"],
1371	        row_count=len(rows),
1372	        violation_row_count=len(
1373	            {index for result in results for index in result["violations"]}
1374	        ),
1375	        results=results,
1376	    )
1377	
1378	    return {
1379	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
1380	        "version": version_row["version"],
1381	        "results": results,
1382	    }

1386	# Quality rule evaluation history (append-only) and read-only diff
1387	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
1388	
1389	
1390	# Serializes read-tail -> append within this process so concurrent evaluations
1391	# never compute the same sequence. SQLite's UNIQUE(version_id, sequence)
1392	# constraint is the hard guard against writers in other processes; such a
1393	# collision is resolved with a bounded re-read-and-retry (mirrors the audit
1394	# record append).
1395	_evaluation_append_locks: dict[int, threading.Lock] = {}
1396	_evaluation_append_locks_guard = threading.Lock()
1397	
1398	# Bound on re-read-and-retry attempts when a writer in another process wins the
1399	# race for the same (version_id, sequence).
1400	_EVALUATION_APPEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 100
1401	
1402	
1403	def _evaluation_append_lock(version_id: int) -> threading.Lock:
1404	    with _evaluation_append_locks_guard:
1405	        lock = _evaluation_append_locks.get(version_id)
1406	        if lock is None:
1407	            lock = threading.Lock()
1408	            _evaluation_append_locks[version_id] = lock
1409	        return lock

1412	def _record_quality_rule_evaluation(
1413	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1414	    version_id: int,
1415	    *,
1416	    row_count: int,
1417	    violation_row_count: int,
1418	    results: list[dict],
1419	) -> None:
1420	    """Append one evaluation summary as the next sequence of the version.
1421	
1422	    The per-version lock makes read-tail -> append atomic within this process
1423	    (FastAPI runs this synchronous endpoint in one process's threadpool). The
1424	    UNIQUE(version_id, sequence) constraint is the hard cross-process guard; a
1425	    writer that loses a race against another process retries with the new tail
1426	    instead of failing the request.
1427	    """
1428	    stored_results = json.dumps(results)
1429	    with _evaluation_append_lock(version_id):
1430	        for attempt in range(_EVALUATION_APPEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS):
1431	            tail = conn.execute(
1432	                "SELECT MAX(sequence) AS max_sequence "
1433	                "FROM quality_rule_evaluations WHERE version_id = ?",
1434	                (version_id,),
1435	            ).fetchone()
1436	            sequence = (tail["max_sequence"] or 0) + 1
1437	            try:
1438	                conn.execute(
1439	                    "INSERT INTO quality_rule_evaluations ("
1440	                    "version_id, sequence, row_count, violation_row_count, "
1441	                    "results, created_at"
1442	                    ") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
1443	                    (
1444	                        version_id,
1445	                        sequence,
1446	                        row_count,
1447	                        violation_row_count,
1448	                        stored_results,
1449	                        utc_now_iso(),
1450	                    ),
1451	                )
1452	                return
1453	            except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
1454	                # Another process inserted the same sequence first. End the
1455	                # current (pinned) transaction so the re-read establishes a new
1456	                # snapshot that includes the competing commit, then retry.
1457	                if attempt + 1 == _EVALUATION_APPEND_MAX_ATTEMPTS:
1458	                    conn.rollback()
1459	                    raise ConflictError(
1460	                        "Too many concurrent evaluation writes; retry the request"
1461	                    )
1462	                conn.rollback()
1463	                continue

1533	def diff_quality_rule_evaluations(
1534	    conn: sqlite3.Connection,
1535	    dataset_name: str,
1536	    version_number: int,
1537	    *,
1538	    body: bytes = b"",
1539	    query_keys: tuple[str, ...] = (),
1540	) -> dict:
1541	    """Read-only diff between the two most recent evaluations of one version.
1542	
1543	    The latest recorded evaluation (``to``) is compared against its immediate
1544	    predecessor (``from``) using exactly the results each of them recorded;
1545	    the persisted rule definitions and submitted rows of the two evaluations
1546	    are all that is consulted. Row positions are the 0-based indices each
1547	    evaluation reported. A rule missing from one side (disabled or not yet
1548	    created between the two evaluations) keeps a null side, and its row-level
1549	    diff fields are null as well, so a missing side stays distinguishable from
1550	    a present side with zero violations. With fewer than two recorded
1551	    evaluations the result is explicitly empty (null sequences, empty lists),
1552	    never an error. Nothing is written.
1553	    """
1554	    dataset, version_row = _require_evaluation_path(
1555	        conn, dataset_name, version_number, body=body, query_keys=query_keys,
1556	        endpoint="evaluation diff",
1557	    )
1558	    rows = conn.execute(
1559	        "SELECT * FROM quality_rule_evaluations WHERE version_id = ? "
1560	        "ORDER BY sequence DESC LIMIT 2",
1561	        (version_row["id"],),
1562	    ).fetchall()
1563	
1564	    empty = {
1565	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
1566	        "version": version_row["version"],
1567	        "from_sequence": None,
1568	        "to_sequence": None,
1569	        "added_violation_rows": [],
1570	        "removed_violation_rows": [],
1571	        "rules": [],
1572	    }
1573	    if len(rows) < 2:
1574	        return empty
1575	
1576	    to_row, from_row = rows[0], rows[1]
1577	    before_results = {r["rule_id"]: r for r in json.loads(from_row["results"])}
1578	    after_results = {r["rule_id"]: r for r in json.loads(to_row["results"])}
1579	
1580	    rule_diffs: list[dict] = []
1581	    for rule_id in sorted(set(before_results) | set(after_results)):
1582	        before = before_results.get(rule_id)
1583	        after = after_results.get(rule_id)
1584	        if before is not None and after is not None:
1585	            before_set = set(before["violations"])
1586	            after_set = set(after["violations"])
1587	            added: list[int] | None = sorted(after_set - before_set)
1588	            removed: list[int] | None = sorted(before_set - after_set)
1589	            delta: int | None = len(after["violations"]) - len(before["violations"])
1590	        else:
1591	            added = removed = delta = None
1592	        rule_diffs.append(
1593	            {
1594	                "rule_id": rule_id,
1595	                "name": (after if after is not None else before)["name"],
1596	                "before": (
1597	                    None
1598	                    if before is None
1599	                    else {
1600	                        "violation_count": len(before["violations"]),
1601	                        "violations": before["violations"],
1602	                    }
1603	                ),
1604	                "after": (
1605	                    None
1606	                    if after is None
1607	                    else {
1608	                        "violation_count": len(after["violations"]),
1609	                        "violations": after["violations"],
1610	                    }
1611	                ),
1612	                "added_violations": added,
1613	                "removed_violations": removed,
1614	                "violation_count_delta": delta,
1615	            }
1616	        )
1617	
1618	    before_rows = {
1619	        index for result in before_results.values() for index in result["violations"]
1620	    }
1621	    after_rows = {
1622	        index for result in after_results.values() for index in result["violations"]
1623	    }
1624	
1625	    return {
1626	        "dataset": dataset["name"],
1627	        "version": version_row["version"],
1628	        "from_sequence": from_row["sequence"],
1629	        "to_sequence": to_row["sequence"],
1630	        "added_violation_rows": sorted(after_rows - before_rows),
1631	        "removed_violation_rows": sorted(before_rows - after_rows),
1632	        "rules": rule_diffs,
1633	    }
